Uploader Files from a dialog or a drop uploader

Shared parts

Several widgets use the same building blocks. You meet them in the widget APIs.

Type Purpose
control_size The Cubit sizes small, medium and large. Controls take it as a constructor argument.
text_role The theme text style of a label or control, such as body or heading_large.
text_tone The semantic color of a label, such as danger or success.
text_line One line of text that remembers its shaping. Custom widgets use it to draw text.
field_text The label, helper text, placeholder and error flag of a form control.
choice_control The base of checkbox, radio_button and toggle. It has a label, helper text, error state and activate().
hover_delay A countdown for tooltips and hover popovers.

Accordion

An accordion is a column of sections. Each section has a heading and content. The user clicks the heading to show or hide the content. Use an accordion for long pages where the user reads one section at a time, such as a list of questions and answers.

Create and configure

Create an accordion and call add_item with a heading and a content widget. add_item returns the accordion_item. You can pass no content and set it later with set_content or emplace_content.

  • set_exclusive(true) lets only one item stay open. By default any number of items stay open.
  • set_appearance picks plain, outlined or filled.
  • set_chevron puts the chevron at the start or the end of the heading.
  • set_size picks a control_size.
  • expand_all() and collapse_all() change every item.

On an item, set_expanded opens or closes it, and toggle() does what a click does. An item can also hold actions at the end of its header. Use set_actions for them.

Events

An item calls the handler from set_on_toggle with the new state after the user opens or closes it. The header is a button. Enter, Space and a click toggle it.

Example

The program examples/widgets/accordion.cpp makes an exclusive accordion of three questions. It opens the second item with a click and prints that the first item closed.

// An accordion where opening one item closes the others.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{320, 176}};

  auto &faq = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::accordion>("Questions");
  faq.set_appearance(basalt::accordion_appearance::outlined);
  faq.set_exclusive(true);
  faq.add_item("What is Basalt?", std::make_unique<basalt::label>("A C++ widget library."));
  faq.add_item("Does it open windows?", std::make_unique<basalt::label>("No. The host does."));
  faq.add_item("Which renderer does it use?", std::make_unique<basalt::label>("Any renderer."));
  faq.item(0).set_expanded(true);
  faq.item(1).set_on_toggle([](bool expanded) {
    std::println("The second item is now {}.", expanded ? "open" : "closed");
  });

  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  host.frame();
  host.click(faq.item(1).header());
  std::println("The first item is {}.", faq.item(0).expanded() ? "open" : "closed");

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Avatar

An avatar is a circle that stands for a person or an entity. It shows a photo when you give it one. Otherwise it shows the initials of the name. The name and a line of supporting text can sit beside the circle.

Create and configure

Pass a name and an optional control_size to the constructor.

  • set_supporting_text adds a second line of text, such as a role.
  • set_image sets a photo. The photo fills the circle.
  • set_layout picks trailing (text after the circle), leading (text before it) or graphic_only. A graphic-only avatar shows the name in a tooltip.
  • diameter() returns the diameter of the circle in layout pixels.

avatar_initials(name) returns the initials that the avatar shows. It takes the first letter of the first and the last word. A single word gives one letter.

Events

An avatar does not handle input. A graphic-only avatar shows its tooltip when the pointer rests on it or when it has keyboard focus.

Example

The program examples/widgets/avatar.cpp shows an avatar with supporting text, a small leading avatar and a large graphic-only avatar. It prints the initials and the diameter.

// Avatars with initials, supporting text, and the three layouts.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{400, 72}};

  auto &row = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::box>(basalt::axis::horizontal);
  row.set_gap(basalt::fixed(24));
  row.set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::center);

  auto &named = row.emplace_child<basalt::avatar>("Grace Hopper");
  named.set_supporting_text("Rear admiral");
  row.emplace_child<basalt::avatar>("Alan Turing", basalt::control_size::small)
      .set_layout(basalt::avatar_layout::leading);
  row.emplace_child<basalt::avatar>("Katherine Johnson", basalt::control_size::large)
      .set_layout(basalt::avatar_layout::graphic_only);

  host.frame();
  std::println("The initials are {}.", basalt::avatar_initials(named.name()));
  std::println("The graphic is {} layout pixels wide.", named.diameter());

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Box

A box places its children in a row or a column. It is the basic layout widget. Most windows are built from nested boxes.

Create and configure

Pass axis::horizontal for a row or axis::vertical for a column. Add children with emplace_child or add_child. These calls use the default item settings.

  • set_gap sets the space between children.
  • set_padding sets the space inside the edges. Use length_insets::uniform for equal padding.
  • set_main_alignment places the children along the box direction when there is spare space.
  • set_cross_alignment places the children across the box direction. The default is stretch.

To change how one child is sized, call add(child, box_item{...}) or set_item. A box_item has these fields:

Field Meaning
grow The share of spare space that the child takes.
shrink The share of a shortage that the child gives up.
basis The size along the box direction before growing or shrinking.
min, max The smallest and the largest size along the box direction.
align The cross alignment of this child.

Lengths are token lengths. Use fixed(16) for 16 token pixels. The display scale and the zoom change the result.

Surface

By default a box paints nothing. set_surface(box_surface{...}) paints a filled, rounded background and a hairline border behind the children. The fill and the border are theme color members, such as &tokens::color_set::background_secondary, so the surface follows the color scheme. The radius is a length. set_surface({}) removes it.

Events

A box does not handle input. Its children receive events as usual.

Notes

A child with grow of 1 in a row takes all spare width. Two children with the same grow share it equally. The example sets the cross alignment of the content to stretch, so the row fills the window.

Example

The program examples/widgets/box.cpp builds a row with a Back button, a title that grows, and a Next button. It prints the width of each child.

// A row in which the middle child takes the spare width.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{400, 72}};

  auto &row = host.content().add(std::make_unique<basalt::box>(basalt::axis::horizontal),
                                 basalt::box_item{.grow = 1});
  row.set_gap(basalt::fixed(8));
  row.set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::center);
  auto &back = row.emplace_child<basalt::button>("Back");
  auto &title = row.add(std::make_unique<basalt::label>("Settings"), basalt::box_item{.grow = 1});
  auto &next = row.emplace_child<basalt::button>("Next");
  title.set_tone(basalt::text_tone::subdued);

  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  host.frame();
  std::println("Back is {} wide, the title is {} wide, and Next is {} wide.",
               back.bounds().extent.width, title.bounds().extent.width, next.bounds().extent.width);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Button

A button starts an action. The user presses it with the pointer, or with Enter or Space while it has focus. The button is a Tab stop, and a click gives it focus.

Create and configure

Pass a label and an optional press handler to the constructor.

  • set_variant picks primary, secondary, tertiary or danger. Use one primary button for the main action of a view. The default is secondary.
  • set_label changes the text.
  • set_label_alignment places the label inside the button. The default is center.
  • set_shortcut sets a text such as Ctrl+S. Assistive technology announces it. Basalt does not bind the key.
  • set_on_press sets the handler.
  • press() does what a click does. It returns false when the button is disabled.

Events

The handler runs when the user releases the primary pointer button over the button, or presses Enter or Space. A disabled button stays focusable and does nothing.

A button that opens a popover calls popover::toggle from its handler. See Popover.

Example

The program examples/widgets/button.cpp shows the four variants in a row. It clicks the primary button and prints the number of presses.

// The four button variants. A simulated click presses the primary button.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{400, 72}};

  auto &row = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::box>(basalt::axis::horizontal);
  row.set_gap(basalt::fixed(8));

  auto presses = 0;
  auto &save = row.emplace_child<basalt::button>("Save");
  save.set_variant(basalt::button_variant::primary);
  save.set_shortcut("Ctrl+S");
  save.set_on_press([&presses] { ++presses; });
  row.emplace_child<basalt::button>("Cancel").set_variant(basalt::button_variant::secondary);
  row.emplace_child<basalt::button>("Skip").set_variant(basalt::button_variant::tertiary);
  row.emplace_child<basalt::button>("Delete").set_variant(basalt::button_variant::danger);

  host.frame();
  host.click(save);
  std::println("The primary button was pressed {} time(s).", presses);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Checkbox

A checkbox is an independent choice with the states unchecked, checked and mixed. Use a checkbox_group for a list of related options. A group can add a select-all checkbox.

Create and configure

For a single box, pass a label, an optional accessibility::check_state and an optional control_size. state() and checked() read the value. set_state changes it.

A checkbox is a choice_control. It also has these functions:

  • set_helper_text shows text below the label. In the error state it holds the error message.
  • set_error turns the error state on or off.
  • activate() does what a click does.

For a group, create a checkbox_group with a name. Call enable_select_all before you add options. Then call add_option for each option. It returns the checkbox. option(index) and checked_count() read the group.

Events

A single box calls the handler from set_on_change with the new check_state. A group calls its handler with the index of the option that changed. Activating a mixed box checks it.

The select-all box is checked when all options are checked. It is mixed when only some are checked. Checking it checks every option.

Example

The program examples/widgets/checkbox.cpp creates a group of three toppings with a select-all box. It clicks the second option and prints the number of checked options.

// A checkbox group with a select-all box. A simulated click checks the second option.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{200, 168}};

  auto &toppings = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::checkbox_group>("Toppings");
  toppings.enable_select_all("All toppings");
  toppings.add_option("Cheese", true);
  toppings.add_option("Mushrooms");
  toppings.add_option("Olives");
  toppings.set_on_change([&toppings](std::size_t index) {
    std::println("{} changed. {} option(s) are checked.", toppings.option(index).label(),
                 toppings.checked_count());
  });

  host.frame();
  host.click(toppings.option(1));

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Chip

A chip is a small pill with a label. Chips show tags, filters and values that the user can remove. A chip can be selectable, removable or both. A chip_group places chips in rows that wrap at the width of the group.

Create and configure

Create a chip_group with a name and a chip_selection: none, single or multiple. With single, selecting a chip deselects the others. Call add_chip to add a chip. It returns the chip.

On a chip:

  • set_selectable(true) lets the user toggle the chip.
  • set_removable(true) shows a remove mark.
  • set_error and set_loading set the error and the busy states. A loading chip ignores input.
  • set_max_width limits the width. A tooltip shows the full label of a shortened chip.
  • toggle() and remove() do what a click does.

On a group, selected_indices() returns the selected chips. set_remove_all_label shows a button that removes all removable chips. remove_all() does the same from code.

Events

A chip calls the handler from set_on_toggle with the new state. It calls the handler from set_on_remove when the user removes it. The Delete and Backspace keys also remove a removable chip. A group calls set_on_change with the index of the chip that changed. A removed chip leaves its group.

Notes

Give a chip group a limited width. In a box, set the cross alignment to stretch, as the example does. Then the chips wrap at the width of the box.

Example

The program examples/widgets/chip.cpp makes a group with multiple selection, clicks the first chip and prints its state.

// A chip group with multiple selection. A simulated click selects the first chip.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{360, 64}};

  auto &filters =
      host.content().emplace_child<basalt::chip_group>("Filters", basalt::chip_selection::multiple);
  filters.add_chip("Open").set_selectable(true);
  filters.add_chip("Closed").set_selectable(true);
  filters.add_chip("Archived").set_removable(true);
  filters.set_on_change([&filters](std::size_t index) {
    std::println("{} is {}.", filters.chip_at(index).label(),
                 filters.chip_at(index).selected() ? "selected" : "not selected");
  });

  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  host.frame();
  host.click(filters.chip_at(0));

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Diagnostics list

A diagnostics list shows problems, one row each. Use it for validation errors, build warnings and notes. The icon of each row has a different shape for errors, warnings and notes. The shape, and not only the color, tells the severity.

Create and configure

Create a diagnostics_list and call set_entries with a vector of diagnostic_entry values. An entry has a severity (error, warning or info), a message and a location. Basalt shows the location but does not read it.

  • set_empty_message sets the text that shows when the list has no entries.
  • focus_row(index) moves keyboard focus to a row. focused_index() reads it.
  • The list is as tall as its rows. Put it in a scroll view to scroll it.

Events

Tab enters the list. Up, Down, Home and End move among the rows. A click, Enter or Space on a row calls the handler from set_on_activate with the row index and its entry. Use it to go to the location in your document.

Example

The program examples/widgets/diagnostics_list.cpp fills a list with three entries, focuses the second row and presses Enter. It prints the location of that entry.

// A list of problems. Keyboard focus moves to a row and Enter activates it.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{360, 128}};

  auto &problems = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::diagnostics_list>();
  problems.set_entries({
      {basalt::diagnostic_severity::error, "Missing closing tag", "document.xml:12:5"},
      {basalt::diagnostic_severity::warning, "Unused style", "styles.xml:3:1"},
      {basalt::diagnostic_severity::info, "Document saved", ""},
  });
  problems.set_on_activate([](std::size_t, basalt::diagnostic_entry const &entry) {
    std::println("Go to {}.", entry.location);
  });

  host.frame();
  problems.focus_row(1);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::enter);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Dialog

A dialog is a message with a title and a row of buttons. It asks the user for a decision, such as whether to discard changes. The dialog shows above the window and blocks the content below it until the user answers.

Create and configure

Pass a title, a message, a list of dialog_button values and an optional cancel index to the constructor. A dialog_button has a label and a button_variant. Show the dialog with overlay_host::show_dialog. That call needs a host above the dialog. See Overlay host.

  • The message wraps at about dialog::wrap_columns characters. Line breaks in the message stay.
  • Focus starts on the first button.
  • choose(index) presses a button from code. It returns false when the index is out of range.

Events

The handler from set_on_choice receives the index of the chosen button. Escape chooses the button at the cancel index.

The dialog does not close itself. In the handler, call overlay_host::dismiss with the identifier that show_dialog returned.

auto const id = host.show_dialog(std::move(shown));
window.set_on_choice([&host, id](std::size_t) { host.dismiss(id); });

The example does not dismiss the dialog, so that the screenshot shows it.

Example

The program examples/widgets/dialog.cpp shows a dialog with a Cancel button and a Discard button. It chooses the second button and prints its index.

// A confirmation dialog in an overlay host. A simulated choice presses the second button.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{480, 200}};

  auto shown = std::make_unique<basalt::dialog>(
      "Discard changes?", "The document has changes that are not saved.",
      std::vector<basalt::dialog_button>{{"Cancel"}, {"Discard", basalt::button_variant::danger}},
      0);
  auto &confirm = *shown;
  confirm.set_on_choice([](std::size_t index) { std::println("Button {} was chosen.", index); });
  host.overlays().show_dialog(std::move(shown));

  host.frame();
  confirm.choose(1);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Image view

An image view shows one picture. It centers the picture in its bounds. It scales the picture down to fit and never makes it larger than its natural size.

Create and configure

Create the view and call set_image with a raster_image_ptr. Make an image from RGBA bytes with raster_image::create(width, height, pixels). Basalt does not decode image files. Decode the file in your program first.

  • set_description sets the text that assistive technology reads in place of the picture. Always set it.
  • set_maximum_height limits the height that the view asks for.
  • image_bounds() returns the rectangle of the picture inside the view. It is empty when the view has no image.

The natural size is one device pixel for each image pixel. On a display with a scale of 2, a 96 pixel image takes 48 layout pixels.

Events

An image view does not handle input.

Example

The program examples/widgets/image_view.cpp builds a gradient in memory, shows it with a maximum height, and prints the size that the picture takes.

// An image built in memory. The view scales it down to fit.

#include <cstdint>
#include <print>
#include <vector>

#include "example_host.h"

namespace {

auto gradient() -> basalt::raster_image_ptr {
  constexpr auto side = std::uint32_t{96};
  auto pixels = std::vector<std::uint8_t>{};
  for (auto y = std::uint32_t{0}; y < side; ++y) {
    for (auto x = std::uint32_t{0}; x < side; ++x) {
      pixels.insert(pixels.end(),
                    {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(x * 2), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(y * 2),
                     std::uint8_t{160}, std::uint8_t{255}});
    }
  }
  return basalt::raster_image::create(side, side, std::move(pixels));
}

} // namespace

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{112, 96}};

  auto &picture = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::image_view>();
  picture.set_image(gradient());
  picture.set_description("A color gradient");
  picture.set_maximum_height(basalt::fixed(64));

  host.frame();
  auto const area = picture.image_bounds();
  std::println("The image fills {} by {} layout pixels.", area.extent.width, area.extent.height);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Label

A label shows one line of text that the user cannot edit. Use it for headings, captions and status text. The label clips its text to its bounds.

Create and configure

Pass the text and an optional text_role to the constructor.

  • set_role picks the theme text style, from body to heading_large. source uses the monospace family.
  • set_tone picks the semantic color: normal, subdued, interactive, danger, warning or success.
  • set_heading_level marks the label as a heading for assistive technology. It does not change the look. Set the role for the look.
  • set_text changes the text.

Events

A label does not handle input.

Notes

A label has one line. To show a longer text, use a multi-line text field in read-only mode. A parent that wants to show all of a label gives it the measured width.

Example

The program examples/widgets/label.cpp shows a heading and four status lines in different tones.

// Labels in different roles and tones.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{320, 176}};

  auto &title = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::label>("Project status",
                                                            basalt::text_role::heading_medium);
  title.set_heading_level(2);
  host.content()
      .emplace_child<basalt::label>("Last build finished a minute ago.")
      .set_tone(basalt::text_tone::subdued);
  host.content()
      .emplace_child<basalt::label>("3 tests passed")
      .set_tone(basalt::text_tone::success);
  host.content().emplace_child<basalt::label>("1 warning").set_tone(basalt::text_tone::warning);
  host.content().emplace_child<basalt::label>("1 test failed").set_tone(basalt::text_tone::danger);

  host.frame();
  std::println("The title is \"{}\".", title.text());

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Menu

A menu is a list of commands. Each item has a label, an optional shortcut hint and an optional check mark. The menu draws its own panel. Whoever shows the menu places it and closes it. menu_bar, select and navigation_bar use menus. You can also show a menu as a context menu with overlay_host::show_popup.

Create and configure

Create a menu with a name. Call add_item(id, label, shortcut, checked) for each command. It returns the menu_item. add_separator() adds a line. find_item(id) returns the item with that identifier or null.

  • A checked value of true or false adds a check column. An empty value makes a plain item.
  • set_shortcut and set_label change an item.
  • activate() on an item does what a click does. It returns false when the item is disabled.

Events

The handler from menu::set_on_activate receives the identifier of the item that the user activated. A click, Enter or Space activates an item. Disabled items stay reachable by keyboard and do nothing. Escape calls the handler from set_on_dismiss. The owner then closes the menu.

The items form one focus group. Tab enters the menu at the item that had focus last. Up, Down, Home and End move among the items and wrap at the ends.

Example

The program examples/widgets/menu.cpp shows a menu with a check item. It clicks the Open item and prints its identifier.

// A menu with a check item. A simulated click activates the Open item.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{200, 192}};

  auto &file = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::menu>("File");
  file.add_item("new", "New", "Ctrl+N");
  file.add_item("open", "Open", "Ctrl+O");
  file.add_separator();
  file.add_item("wrap", "Wrap lines", "", true);
  file.add_item("quit", "Quit", "Ctrl+Q");
  file.set_on_activate([](std::string const &id) { std::println("The command is {}.", id); });

  host.frame();
  host.click(*file.find_item("open"));

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Menu bar

A menu bar is a row of menu titles along the top of a window. The user chooses a title to open its menu below the title. The bar opens menus in the nearest overlay_host, so the window needs one.

Create and configure

Create a menu_bar and call add_menu(title, populate) for each title. The bar calls populate with an empty menu each time the menu opens. Build the items in that function. Then the enabled and the checked states are always current.

  • open_menu(index) opens a menu from code. It returns false when the index is out of range or the bar has no host.
  • close_menu() closes the open menu. is_open() tells whether a menu is open.
  • set_menu_visible(index, false) hides a title. A hidden menu is skipped by layout and focus.

Events

Choosing an item closes the menu. Then the bar calls the handler from set_on_command with the identifier of the item. Tab enters the bar. Left and Right move among the titles. Enter or Space opens the focused title.

Example

The program examples/widgets/menu_bar.cpp makes a bar with two menus and opens the File menu.

// A menu bar. The program opens the File menu, which is built when it opens.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{320, 176}};

  auto &bar = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::menu_bar>();
  bar.add_menu("File", [](basalt::menu &file) {
    file.add_item("new", "New", "Ctrl+N");
    file.add_item("open", "Open", "Ctrl+O");
    file.add_item("quit", "Quit", "Ctrl+Q");
  });
  bar.add_menu("View", [](basalt::menu &view) { view.add_item("wrap", "Wrap lines", "", true); });
  bar.set_on_command([](std::string const &id) { std::println("The command is {}.", id); });

  host.frame();
  bar.open_menu(0);
  host.frame();
  std::println("The menu is {}.", bar.is_open() ? "open" : "closed");

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Navigation bar

A navigation bar runs across the top of an application. The sections layout shows leading actions, a title, navigation sections, center actions, utility links and an avatar. The toolbar layout shows only the title and the actions.

Create and configure

Create a navigation_bar with a name for assistive technology.

  • set_title sets the title.
  • add_section(id, label) adds a destination and returns its navigation_item. Call add_entry(id, label) on the item to give it a submenu. An item with entries opens the submenu instead of navigating.
  • add_utility_link(id, label) adds a link such as Help.
  • emplace_leading<T>() and emplace_center<T>() add widgets to the leading and center areas.
  • set_avatar sets the avatar at the end.
  • set_layout picks sections or toolbar.
  • select(id) marks a destination as selected without calling the handler. selected_id() reads it.

Events

The handler from set_on_navigate receives the identifier of the section, the submenu entry or the utility link that the user chose. Sections and their entries also become the selected destination.

Example

The program examples/widgets/navigation_bar.cpp builds a bar with two sections, a utility link and an avatar. It clicks Home and prints the selected destination.

// A navigation bar with sections, a utility link and an avatar. A simulated click chooses Home.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{640, 80}};

  auto &bar = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::navigation_bar>("Main navigation");
  bar.set_title("Basalt");
  bar.add_section("home", "Home");
  bar.add_section("docs", "Docs").add_entry("api", "API reference");
  bar.add_utility_link("help", "Help");
  bar.set_avatar(std::make_unique<basalt::avatar>("Ada Lovelace", basalt::control_size::small));
  bar.set_on_navigate([](std::string const &id) { std::println("Navigate to {}.", id); });

  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  host.frame();
  host.click(*bar.find_item("home"));
  std::println("The selected destination is {}.", bar.selected_id().value_or("none"));

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Overlay host

An overlay host is the root widget of a window. It holds one content widget that fills the window. It also shows popups and dialogs above the content.

A widget clips its children to its own bounds. A menu that opens below a button must go beyond the bounds of the button, so it is shown in the host instead.

Create and configure

Make the host the root of the tree with tree.emplace_root<overlay_host>(). Call set_content with the widget that holds your window. content() returns it.

Function Result
show_popup(widget, anchor, on_close) Shows a popup below the anchor rectangle, or above it when it does not fit. A press outside the popup, or Escape, closes it. The popup blocks the content below and traps focus.
show_hover_popup(widget, anchor, on_close) Shows a popup that does not block input. Only dismiss and dismiss_all close it. Tooltips use it.
show_dialog(widget, on_close) Shows the widget in the center over a dimmed window. The owner or Escape closes it.
make_exclusive(id) Dismisses the previous exclusive overlay. Popovers use it.
dismiss(id) Closes one overlay. It returns false when the overlay is already gone.
dismiss_all() Closes every overlay.

Each show function returns a widget_id. is_open(id) and overlay_count() report the state. overlay_host::find(widget) returns the nearest host above a widget, or null.

The on_close handler runs once when the overlay goes away, whichever way. Overlays stack. The most recent one is on top.

Events

The host sends pointer and keyboard input to the top overlay first. A modal overlay stops the pointer from reaching the content below it.

Example

The program examples/widgets/overlay_host.cpp shows a menu in a popup below a button. It prints the number of overlays and then dismisses the popup.

// A popup menu shown in the overlay host, below an anchor rectangle.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{240, 176}};

  auto &more = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::button>("More");
  host.frame();

  auto actions = std::make_unique<basalt::menu>("More actions");
  actions->add_item("rename", "Rename");
  actions->add_item("duplicate", "Duplicate");
  actions->add_item("delete", "Delete");
  auto const popup = host.overlays().show_popup(std::move(actions), more.bounds_in_root(),
                                                [] { std::println("The popup closed."); });
  host.frame();
  std::println("{} overlay(s) are open.", host.overlays().overlay_count());

  auto const status = host.finish(argc, argv);
  host.overlays().dismiss(popup);
  return status;
}

Palette

A palette is a search box above a short list of choices. Use it for a command palette or a quick switcher. Show it with overlay_host::show_dialog.

Create and configure

Create a palette. Call set_entries with a vector of palette_entry values. An entry has an id, a label, a detail (such as a key binding), a category, a state and a dimmed flag. A dimmed entry is drawn in muted colors and can still be chosen.

The palette does not filter. It reports each change of the query. You answer with set_entries, already ranked. At most palette::visible_rows entries show. The list scrolls to keep the selection in view.

  • set_placeholder sets the hint text of the search box.
  • set_query changes the query without calling the handler.
  • set_empty_message sets the text for an empty list.
  • focus_query() moves focus to the search box. Call it after you show the palette.
  • select(index), move_selection(delta) and choose_selected() work from code.

Events

The handler from set_on_query_change receives the new query after each edit. The handler from set_on_choose receives the identifier of the chosen entry. A click on a row, or Enter, chooses an entry. Up, Down, Page Up and Page Down move the selection. Focus stays in the search box.

The palette does not close itself. The choice handler runs first. Then you dismiss the overlay.

Example

The program examples/widgets/palette.cpp shows a palette, filters the entries as the user types, and chooses the selected entry.

// A command palette. The owner filters the entries when the query changes.

#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>
#include <print>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "example_host.h"

namespace {

auto commands() -> std::vector<basalt::palette_entry> {
  return {
      {.id = "theme", .label = "Toggle theme", .detail = "Ctrl+T", .category = "View"},
      {.id = "dialog", .label = "Show dialog", .category = "Window"},
      {.id = "save", .label = "Save file", .detail = "Ctrl+S", .category = "File"},
      {.id = "save_all", .label = "Save all files", .category = "File"},
  };
}

auto matching(std::string query) -> std::vector<basalt::palette_entry> {
  std::ranges::transform(query, query.begin(),
                         [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
  auto result = std::vector<basalt::palette_entry>{};
  for (auto &entry : commands()) {
    auto label = entry.label;
    std::ranges::transform(label, label.begin(),
                           [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
    if (label.contains(query)) {
      result.push_back(std::move(entry));
    }
  }
  return result;
}

} // namespace

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{640, 240}};

  auto shown = std::make_unique<basalt::palette>();
  auto &palette = *shown;
  palette.set_placeholder("Type a command");
  palette.set_entries(commands());
  palette.set_on_query_change(
      [&palette](std::string const &query) { palette.set_entries(matching(query)); });
  palette.set_on_choose([](std::string const &id) { std::println("The command is {}.", id); });
  host.overlays().show_dialog(std::move(shown));

  host.frame();
  palette.focus_query();
  host.type("save");
  std::println("{} entries match.", palette.entries().size());
  palette.choose_selected();

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Popover

A popover is a trigger widget with a panel that shows beside it. A hover popover shows short text when the pointer rests on the trigger. A click popover shows content that the user can operate.

Create and configure

Create a popover with a popover_trigger: hover or click. Set the trigger widget with emplace_trigger<T>() or set_trigger. Then set the content.

  • set_text shows plain text.
  • set_content takes a function that builds the content widget. The popover calls it each time it opens.
  • set_tip(true) shows a tip that points at the trigger.
  • set_hover_delay sets how long the pointer must rest before a hover popover opens.
  • open(), close() and toggle() work from code. open() returns false when there is no content, no host or the popover is disabled.
  • is_open() reads the state.

The panel opens below the trigger, or above it when it does not fit. Only one popover is open in a host at a time. Opening one closes another. The popover needs an overlay host above it.

Events

set_on_visibility_changed calls its handler with true when the panel opens and false when it closes. A click popover takes focus when it opens. An outside press or Escape closes it.

A trigger that handles clicks itself, such as a button, must call toggle from its own handler. A trigger that leaves clicks unhandled, such as a label, needs no handler.

Example

The program examples/widgets/popover.cpp makes a click popover with a button trigger. It clicks the button and prints that the popover opened.

// A popover that opens when its button trigger is clicked.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{280, 120}};

  auto &details = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::popover>(basalt::popover_trigger::click);
  auto &trigger = details.emplace_trigger<basalt::button>("Details");
  trigger.set_on_press([&details] { details.toggle(); });
  details.set_text("The build ran on three machines.");
  details.set_on_visibility_changed(
      [](bool open) { std::println("The popover {}.", open ? "opened" : "closed"); });

  host.frame();
  host.click(trigger);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Progress bar

A progress bar shows how far an operation has come. A bar with a fraction fills from the left. A bar without a fraction is indeterminate. It shows a short segment that moves along the track.

Create and configure

Pass a fraction from 0 to 1 to the constructor, or pass nothing for an indeterminate bar.

  • set_fraction changes the value. It clamps values outside 0 to 1. Pass std::nullopt to make the bar indeterminate.
  • tick(step) moves the indeterminate segment by step of the track width and repaints. Call it once per frame while the operation runs. On a bar with a fraction, tick only repaints.
  • fraction() reads the value.

Events

A progress bar does not handle input. Assistive technology reads the fraction.

Example

The program examples/widgets/progress_bar.cpp shows a determinate bar and an indeterminate bar. It moves the second bar one step and prints both states.

// A determinate bar and an indeterminate bar that moves each time `tick` runs.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{320, 64}};

  auto &upload = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::progress_bar>(std::optional<float>{0.6F});
  auto &waiting = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::progress_bar>();
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  upload.set_fraction(0.75F);
  waiting.tick(0.3F);
  host.frame();
  std::println("The upload is {:.0f} percent done.", *upload.fraction() * 100);
  std::println("The second bar is {}.", waiting.fraction() ? "determinate" : "indeterminate");

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Radio button

Radio buttons let the user choose one option from a set. Choosing an option clears the others. A radio_group holds the options and enforces this rule.

Create and configure

Create a radio_group with a name and an optional axis. Call add_option(label) for each option. It returns the radio_button.

  • select(index) selects an option from code and clears the others. It returns false when the index is out of range.
  • selected_index() returns the selected index, or an empty value.
  • option(index) returns one option.
  • option_count() returns the number of options.

An option is a choice_control. It has set_helper_text, set_error and set_size. Call set_selected on a single option only when you manage the group yourself.

Events

The handler from set_on_change receives the index of the option that the user chose. The group is one Tab stop. Tab enters it at the selected option. The arrow keys move focus to the next option and select it.

Example

The program examples/widgets/radio_button.cpp creates a group of three sizes, clicks the last option and prints the label of the selected option.

// A radio group. A simulated click selects the third option.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{160, 144}};

  auto &size = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::radio_group>("Size");
  size.add_option("Small");
  size.add_option("Medium");
  size.add_option("Large");
  size.select(1);
  size.set_on_change(
      [&size](std::size_t index) { std::println("{} is selected.", size.option(index).label()); });

  host.frame();
  host.click(size.option(2));

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Scroll bar

A scroll bar is a track with a thumb. It does not scroll anything. It reports the offset that the user asks for, and its owner applies it. A scroll_view can create scroll bars for you. Create one yourself only to scroll custom content.

Create and configure

Pass an axis to the constructor. Call set_metrics(content, viewport, offset) with the full scrollable length, the visible length and the start of the visible part. All values are in layout pixels along the axis.

  • thumb_rect() returns the thumb rectangle. It is empty when nothing scrolls.
  • max_offset() returns the largest offset.
  • scroll_bar::default_thickness is the usual thickness of a bar.

Events

set_on_scroll calls its handler with the offset that the user asks for. Basalt clamps the offset to 0 and max_offset(). In the handler, apply the offset and call set_metrics again.

The user drags the thumb, or presses the track beside it to move one page toward the press. The bar is not a Tab stop. The scrolled content handles keys. Assistive technology uses the increment and decrement actions.

Example

The program examples/widgets/scroll_bar.cpp creates a horizontal bar and presses the track after the thumb. It prints the offset that the bar asks for.

// A horizontal scroll bar. A press on the track beside the thumb pages toward the press.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{320, 44}};

  auto &bar = host.content().add(std::make_unique<basalt::scroll_bar>(basalt::axis::horizontal),
                                 basalt::box_item{.basis = basalt::scroll_bar::default_thickness});
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  bar.set_metrics(1000, 250, 0);
  bar.set_on_scroll([&bar](float offset) {
    std::println("The bar asks for offset {}.", offset);
    bar.set_metrics(1000, 250, offset);
  });

  host.frame();
  auto const thumb = bar.thumb_rect();
  host.click_at({bar.bounds_in_root().right() - 8, bar.bounds_in_root().center().y});
  std::println("The thumb is {} layout pixels wide.", thumb.extent.width);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Scroll view

A scroll view shows a window onto content that is larger than the view. The content is one widget. Along each scrolling axis, the content takes the size it needs. Along the other axis, it matches the view.

Create and configure

Pass a scroll_axes value to the constructor: vertical, horizontal or both. Set the content with emplace_content<T>() or set_content.

  • set_scrollbars(true) adds scroll bars. A bar shows only while the content overflows.
  • scroll_by(delta) and set_scroll_offset(offset) move the content at once. They return true when the offset changed.
  • scroll_into_view(rect) scrolls as little as possible to show a rectangle in content coordinates.
  • scroll_offset(), max_scroll_offset(), content_size() and visible_content_rect() read the state.
  • set_focus_policy(focus_policy::tab) makes the view a Tab stop, so keys scroll it.

You can request an offset before layout. The view keeps it and clamps it when it knows the size of the content.

Events

The wheel always scrolls. Each wheel event moves a target, and the view eases toward it over the next frames. Key presses, scroll bars and calls from code move the content at once. A focused view scrolls with the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End.

Example

The program examples/widgets/scroll_view.cpp puts twenty labels in a vertical scroll view with scroll bars, scrolls down by 60 layout pixels and prints the offset.

// A scroll view with scroll bars over a column of labels.

#include <format>
#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{240, 168}};

  auto &view =
      host.content().add(std::make_unique<basalt::scroll_view>(basalt::scroll_axes::vertical),
                         basalt::box_item{.basis = basalt::fixed(136)});
  view.set_scrollbars(true);
  auto &rows = view.emplace_content<basalt::box>(basalt::axis::vertical);
  for (auto number = 1; number <= 20; ++number) {
    rows.emplace_child<basalt::label>(std::format("Row {}", number));
  }
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  host.frame();
  view.scroll_by({0, 60});
  host.frame();
  std::println("The view shows content from y = {}.", view.scroll_offset().y);
  std::println("The content is {:.0f} layout pixels tall.", view.content_size().height);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Select

A select shows the chosen value, or a placeholder, in a field. It opens a list of options in a popup. The single mode chooses one option. The multiple mode chooses several. A label shows above the field. Helper text or an error message shows below it.

Create and configure

Pass a label and an optional control_size to the constructor. Call add_option(label) for each option.

  • set_mode picks select_mode::single or select_mode::multiple.
  • set_placeholder sets the text that shows when nothing is chosen.
  • set_helper_text sets the text below the field. set_error(true) makes it an error message.
  • choose(index, chosen) changes the choice from code. clear() removes it.
  • chosen_indices() and is_chosen(index) read the choice. option_label(index) returns the label of an option.
  • open() and close() work from code. open() returns false when the select is disabled, has no options or has no host.

The select needs an overlay host above it.

Events

set_on_change calls its handler without arguments after the user changes the choice. Read the new choice with chosen_indices(). Enter, Space and Down open the list. In multiple mode, the field shows how many options are chosen, and the list stays open while the user toggles options. Delete and Backspace clear the choice.

Example

The program examples/widgets/select.cpp creates a select with four options, opens it, moves the choice to the third option with the keyboard and prints the choice.

// A single-choice select. The program opens the list and moves the choice with the keyboard.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{240, 216}};

  auto &language = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::select>("Language");
  language.set_placeholder("Choose one");
  for (auto const *name : {"C++", "C#", "Go", "TypeScript"}) {
    language.add_option(name);
  }
  language.set_helper_text("Used for new projects");
  language.set_on_change([&language] {
    std::println("{} is chosen.", language.option_label(language.chosen_indices().front()));
  });

  host.frame();
  host.click(language);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::down);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::down);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::enter);
  host.click(language);
  std::println("The list is {}.", language.is_open() ? "open" : "closed");

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Separator

A separator is a thin line between groups of controls. A horizontal separator runs from left to right and stretches across its parent. A vertical separator runs from top to bottom.

Create and configure

Pass an axis to the constructor. The default is axis::horizontal. set_direction changes it.

A separator takes the width of its parent only when the parent stretches its children. In a box, set the cross alignment to stretch.

Events

A separator does not handle input.

Example

The program examples/widgets/separator.cpp puts a separator between two labels and prints its width.

// A separator between two groups of controls.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{280, 104}};

  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  host.content().emplace_child<basalt::label>("Account");
  auto &rule = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::separator>();
  host.content().emplace_child<basalt::label>("Notifications");

  host.frame();
  std::println("The separator is {} wide.", rule.bounds().extent.width);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Split view

A split view has two panes with a divider between them. With axis::horizontal the panes sit side by side. With axis::vertical they are stacked. The user can drag the divider when the view is resizable.

Create and configure

Pass an axis to the constructor. Set the panes with set_first and set_second. When only one pane is present, it fills the view and there is no divider.

Choose what stays constant when the view changes size:

Call Anchor Meaning
set_ratio(r) proportional The first pane keeps the fraction r of the space.
set_first_length(length) first The first pane keeps its length.
set_second_length(length) second The second pane keeps its length.
  • set_minimums(first, second) sets the smallest pane lengths. The view enforces them on every layout. When both do not fit, the first minimum wins.
  • set_divider_thickness sets the thickness of the visible line.
  • move_divider_to(position) and move_divider_by(delta) move the divider. They return the position after the minimums apply.
  • divider_rect() returns the divider as of the last layout.

Events

set_resizable(true) adds a splitter over the divider. handle() returns it. The splitter is wider than the visible line, so that the user can grab it. A pointer press on it starts a drag. The splitter is a Tab stop. The arrow keys move the divider by splitter::key_step. Home and End move it to the limits.

You do not create a splitter yourself.

Example

The program examples/widgets/split_view.cpp makes a resizable view with a first pane of fixed length. It moves the divider by one step and prints the position before and after.

// A resizable split view. The program moves the divider by a step.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{420, 152}};

  auto &split = host.content().add(std::make_unique<basalt::split_view>(basalt::axis::horizontal),
                                   basalt::box_item{.basis = basalt::fixed(120)});
  split.set_first(std::make_unique<basalt::label>("Files"));
  split.set_second(std::make_unique<basalt::label>("Editor"));
  split.set_first_length(basalt::fixed(120));
  split.set_minimums(basalt::fixed(80), basalt::fixed(80));
  split.set_resizable(true);
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  host.frame();
  std::println("The divider starts at x = {}.", split.divider_rect().origin.x);
  split.move_divider_by(basalt::splitter::key_step.value);
  std::println("The divider is now at x = {}.", split.divider_rect().origin.x);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Stack

A stack layers its children on top of each other. Children are painted in the order that you add them, so the last child is on top. Use a stack for a badge over an icon, or a placeholder over an empty editor.

Create and configure

Add a child with add(child, stack_item{...}). A stack_item has a horizontal and a vertical alignment. A child that does not stretch keeps its measured size, limited to the content rectangle. emplace_child uses the default item, which stretches the child.

  • set_padding insets the content rectangle.
  • set_item(child, item) changes the placement of a child. It returns false when the widget is not a child of the stack.

Events

A stack does not handle input. Its children receive events as usual. The top child is hit first.

Example

The program examples/widgets/stack.cpp puts a New chip on the top right corner of an avatar and prints the size of the stack.

// A badge layered over the corner of an avatar.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{80, 80}};

  auto &badged = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::stack>();
  auto &person =
      badged.emplace_child<basalt::avatar>("Margaret Hamilton", basalt::control_size::large);
  person.set_layout(basalt::avatar_layout::graphic_only);
  badged.add(std::make_unique<basalt::chip>("New", basalt::control_size::small),
             basalt::stack_item{.horizontal = basalt::alignment::end,
                                .vertical = basalt::alignment::start});

  host.frame();
  std::println("The stack is {} by {} layout pixels.", badged.bounds().extent.width,
               badged.bounds().extent.height);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Status bar

A status bar is a row of text sections along the bottom of a window. Typical sections are a message, the caret position and the encoding.

Create and configure

Call add_section(id, text, grow) for each section. It returns the label of the section. A section with grow above zero takes the spare width. It pushes the sections after it to the right edge.

  • set_section_text(id, text) changes a section. It returns false when no section has that identifier.
  • section(id) returns the label, or null.
  • set_name sets the name for assistive technology.

Events

A status bar does not handle input. It is a polite live region. Assistive technology announces changes to its sections without moving focus.

Example

The program examples/widgets/status_bar.cpp makes a bar with a growing message and two fixed sections, updates two sections and prints the message.

// A status bar. The first section grows and pushes the others to the right.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{480, 64}};

  auto &status = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::status_bar>();
  status.add_section("message", "Ready", 1);
  status.add_section("position", "Ln 1, Col 1");
  status.add_section("encoding", "UTF-8");
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  status.set_section_text("message", "Saved");
  status.set_section_text("position", "Ln 12, Col 5");
  host.frame();
  std::println("The message section reads \"{}\".", status.section("message")->text());

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Tabs

A tab bar is a row of tabs. The user picks one tab to choose a view. The bar reports the selection. Your program shows the matching content. The bar does not hold the content.

Create and configure

Create a tab_bar with a name. Call add_tab(label) for each tab. It returns the tab.

  • select(index) selects a tab and clears the others. It returns false when the index is out of range. Unlike most setters, it calls the select handler when the selection changed.
  • selected_index() returns the selected index, or an empty value.
  • tab_at(index) and tab_count() read the tabs.
  • tab::set_closable(true) shows a close button at the end of a tab.
  • scroll_tab_into_view(index) scrolls a long row to show a tab.
  • set_style(tab_bar_style::segmented) changes the look, as described below.

Tabs shrink toward a minimum width as the row fills. When they no longer fit, the row scrolls sideways. The wheel or the trackpad scrolls it. A vertical wheel turns sideways.

Overflow controls

When the tabs do not fit, the bar shows a fade at each edge that has more tabs past it and a scroll button at each end. A scroll button moves the row just far enough to show the next partly hidden tab, and repeats while held. If an overlay_host is above the bar, a third button opens a menu of every tab. Choosing an item selects the tab and scrolls it into view. Without a host, the bar shows no menu button.

The buttons paint the bar’s background so that no tab shows beneath them. Call set_background(&tokens::color_set::background_secondary) when the bar sits on a different color. The buttons are not Tab stops. Left and Right scroll the row as they select, and Down on a tab opens the menu. scroll_toward_start(), scroll_toward_end() and open_tab_menu() do the same from code.

Segmented style

set_style(tab_bar_style::segmented) divides the width equally among the tabs inside a rounded group. The bar never scrolls and shows no overflow controls. Labels that do not fit are shortened in the middle. Use it for a few options, such as a mode switch. Selection, focus and keyboard behavior are the same as in the default line style.

Events

set_on_select calls its handler with the index of the newly selected tab. set_on_close calls its handler with the index of a tab whose close button the user pressed. The bar does not remove the tab. Remove or rebuild the tabs in the handler.

The tabs form one focus group. Tab enters at the selected tab. Left, Right, Home and End move among the tabs and select as they go.

Example

The program examples/widgets/tabs.cpp makes a bar with three tabs, one of them closable. It clicks the second tab and prints the selection.

// A tab bar with more tabs than fit. It shows the scroll buttons, and a simulated click on the
// trailing button scrolls the row.

#include <print>
#include <string>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{420, 72}};

  auto &sections = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::tab_bar>("Sections");
  for (int i = 1; i <= 8; ++i) {
    sections.add_tab("Section " + std::to_string(i)).set_closable(i == 8);
  }
  sections.select(0);
  sections.set_on_select([](std::size_t index) { std::println("Tab {} is selected.", index); });
  sections.set_on_close([](std::size_t index) { std::println("Tab {} asked to close.", index); });

  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);
  host.frame();
  sections.scroll_toward_end();
  host.frame();
  std::println("The row is scrolled {} pixels of {}.", sections.scroll_offset(),
               sections.max_scroll_offset());

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Text field

A text field is editable text for dialogs, search boxes and other short input. It has a single-line form and a multi-line form.

Create and configure

Pass the initial text and a multiline flag to the constructor.

  • set_text replaces the content without calling the change handler. The caret goes to the end.
  • set_placeholder sets the text that shows when the field is empty.
  • set_read_only(true) blocks edits. The user can still select and copy.
  • set_accessible_name sets the name that assistive technology reads, such as “Find”. Set it for every field.
  • set_framed(false) removes the background and the border, for a field inside an editor view.
  • set_role picks a text style, such as source.
  • set_preferred_width sets the width that the field wants when its parent does not limit it.
  • set_clipboard gives the field a text_clipboard with read and write functions. The shortcuts for copy, cut and paste work only when you set both.

To work with the selection, use selection(), selected_text(), set_selection(anchor, focus) and select_all(). insert_text replaces the selection as typing does. All offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets on grapheme boundaries.

Events

set_on_change calls its handler with the new text after each edit by the user or by assistive technology. set_on_submit calls its handler when the user presses Enter in a single-line field.

A single-line field never wraps. It turns line breaks in inserted text into spaces and scrolls sideways to keep the caret in view. A multi-line field wraps at its width and grows with its content. Inside a scroll view, it scrolls the caret into view.

The caret moves by grapheme. Alt or Ctrl moves it by word. Shift extends the selection. The field shows input method composition in place, with an underline. The field has no undo. Keep the history in your editor.

Commit a value

Use these handlers for a field that has no confirm button.

  • set_on_focus_lost calls its handler with the text when the field loses focus after an edit that Enter did not confirm. Focus moves away when the user presses Tab, clicks another widget, or hides the field, or when a modal opens.
  • set_on_cancel calls its handler when the user presses Escape. Usually the handler calls set_text with the stored value. While you set this handler, the field takes the Escape key. A dialog that contains the field does not close on Escape until focus leaves the field. During input method composition, Escape goes to the input method and the handler is not called.
  • has_unconfirmed_edit() is true after an edit that Enter, Escape, set_text or a focus-lost call has not ended.

The field does not call the focus-lost handler in these cases:

  • The window becomes inactive. The field keeps its focus and its edit.
  • The field leaves the widget tree. Before you remove a field, read has_unconfirmed_edit() and commit the text yourself.
  • The field is read-only.

A handler can remove the field from the tree.

Example

The program examples/widgets/text_field.cpp makes a single-line field and a read-only multi-line field. It clicks the first field, types a name and presses Enter.

// A single-line field that receives typed text, and a read-only multi-line field.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{320, 128}};

  auto &name = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::text_field>();
  name.set_placeholder("Your name");
  name.set_accessible_name("Name");
  name.set_on_change([](std::string const &text) { std::println("The text is \"{}\".", text); });
  name.set_on_submit([](std::string const &text) { std::println("Submitted \"{}\".", text); });
  auto &notes = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::text_field>(
      "A multi-line field wraps at its width.", true);
  notes.set_accessible_name("Notes");
  notes.set_read_only(true);
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  host.frame();
  host.click(name);
  host.type("Ada");
  host.press_key(basalt::key::enter);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Toggle

A toggle is an on/off switch. Its effect is immediate, like a light switch. Use a checkbox for a choice that the user confirms later.

Create and configure

Pass a label, an initial state and an optional control_size to the constructor.

  • set_on changes the state without calling the handler. on() reads it.
  • set_status_text(off_text, on_text) shows the text for the current state after the label. clear_status_text() removes it.
  • set_helper_text shows text below the label.

A toggle has no error state and no mixed state.

Events

set_on_change calls its handler with the new state after the user changes it. A click or Space changes the state. The toggle is a Tab stop.

Example

The program examples/widgets/toggle.cpp makes two toggles with status text. It clicks the second toggle and prints its new state.

// Two toggles. A simulated click switches Bluetooth on.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{200, 96}};

  auto &wifi = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::toggle>("Wi-Fi", true);
  wifi.set_status_text("Off", "On");
  auto &bluetooth = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::toggle>("Bluetooth");
  bluetooth.set_status_text("Off", "On");
  bluetooth.set_on_change([](bool on) { std::println("Bluetooth is {}.", on ? "on" : "off"); });

  host.frame();
  host.click(bluetooth);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Tooltip

A tooltip is a short hint on a dark bubble. It names a control that has no visible text, or it explains a shortened text. tooltip is the bubble. tooltip_anchor is the part that decides when to show it.

Create and configure

Use tooltip_anchor inside your own widget. The built-in avatar and chip do so. The anchor shows the tooltip after the pointer rests on the widget, or after the widget takes visible keyboard focus. It hides the tooltip when the pointer leaves, when the focus ring goes away, when the text becomes empty or when the widget detaches.

  1. Add a tooltip_anchor member to the widget.
  2. Call set_text(*this, text) to set the hint.
  3. Call update(*this) from on_interaction_changed. When it returns true, call request_animation_frame.
  4. Call advance(*this, elapsed) from on_animation_frame and return its result.
  5. Call hide(*this) from on_detached.

The constructor takes a delay. The default is 500 milliseconds. visible() tells whether the tooltip shows. Without an overlay host above the widget, nothing shows.

To show a tooltip without an anchor, call overlay_host::show_hover_popup with a tooltip and the bounds of the widget. The example does this.

Events

A tooltip does not handle input. Its bubble is non-modal, so the pointer passes through it.

Example

The program examples/widgets/tooltip.cpp shows a tooltip below a button with a hover popup and prints that it is visible.

// A tooltip shown above a button, as a hover popup. The pointer rests on the button first.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{240, 112}};

  auto &save = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::button>("Save");
  host.content().set_padding(basalt::length_insets::uniform(basalt::fixed(40)));
  host.frame();

  auto const bubble = host.overlays().show_hover_popup(
      std::make_unique<basalt::tooltip>("Save the document"), save.bounds_in_root());
  host.frame();
  std::println("The tooltip is {}.", host.overlays().is_open(bubble) ? "visible" : "hidden");

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Tree view

A tree view shows nested rows that the user can expand and collapse. Use it for an outline, a folder tree or any other hierarchy. The tree makes widgets only for the rows that you can see. Thus a tree with many thousands of rows costs about the same as a tree with a few rows.

Create and configure

Create a tree_view with an accessible name. Call set_rows with a tree_rows value. It holds two functions: count gives the number of rows, and row gives the tree_row at an index. The rows are the visible rows in display order. The descendants of a collapsed row are not rows.

A tree_row has these fields:

  • text: the label of the row.
  • detail: secondary text. The tree shows it at the end of the row in a subdued color.
  • depth: 0 for a top-level row.
  • expandable and expanded: whether the row has a chevron, and which way it points.
  • position_in_set and set_size: the position of the row among its siblings, and their count. Assistive technology uses them. Set them when you know them, because the tree cannot count rows that it did not make.

tree_rows has a third, optional function, depth. It gives the depth of a row without its text. The tree uses it when it walks over many rows, for example to find the parent of a row.

The tree keeps no copy of your data. When the data changes, call rows_changed().

  • select(index) selects a row, and select(std::nullopt) clears the selection. The tree does not scroll, and it does not take focus. If focus is in the tree, focus moves to the new row.
  • selected() gives the selected row.
  • scroll_to_row(index) scrolls as little as possible to show the row.
  • row_area(index) gives the area of a row in the coordinates of the tree.

The tree has no natural width. Give it a width with its layout, for example with set_cross_alignment(alignment::stretch) on the parent box. Give it a limited height, because it scrolls only when its rows are taller than the tree.

Events

Your program owns the expanded state. When the user asks to expand or collapse a row, the tree calls the handler from set_on_expand with the row index and the new state. The handler must change the data and call rows_changed(). The selection moves with the change: a row below the subtree keeps its selection, and a hidden row gives its selection to the collapsed row.

The rows are one Tab stop. These keys move the selection and call the handler from set_on_select:

  • Up and Down move one row. Page Up and Page Down move one page. Home and End move to the first and last rows.
  • Right expands a collapsed row. On an expanded row, Right moves to the first child.
  • Left collapses an expanded row. On another row, Left moves to the parent.
  • Typed text moves to the next row whose text starts with that text. After a pause of one second, a new search starts.

A click selects a row. A click on the chevron also expands or collapses the row. Enter and a double click call the handler from set_on_activate.

Example

The program examples/widgets/tree_view.cpp shows a tree of folders and files. It moves to the docs row, expands it, selects the file in it and opens the file.

// A tree of folders and files. The program owns the expanded state, and the tree asks it for the
// rows it shows.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <print>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "example_host.h"

namespace {

struct entry {
  std::string name;
  std::uint32_t depth = 0;
  bool expanded = false;
};

// The entries in pre-order.
std::vector<entry> entries{
    {"src", 0, true}, {"main.cpp", 1}, {"tree.cpp", 1},
    {"docs", 0},      {"guide.md", 1}, {"README.md", 0},
};

auto has_children(std::size_t i) -> bool {
  return i + 1 < entries.size() && entries[i + 1].depth > entries[i].depth;
}

// The entry behind each row. A collapsed entry hides its descendants.
auto shown() -> std::vector<std::size_t> {
  std::vector<std::size_t> rows;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < entries.size();) {
    rows.push_back(i);
    std::size_t next = i + 1;
    while (!entries[i].expanded && next < entries.size() &&
           entries[next].depth > entries[i].depth) {
      ++next;
    }
    i = next;
  }
  return rows;
}

} // namespace

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{240, 180}};
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  auto &tree = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::tree_view>("Files");
  tree.set_rows({
      .count = [] { return shown().size(); },
      .row =
          [](std::size_t index) {
            std::size_t const i = shown()[index];
            return basalt::tree_row{.text = entries[i].name,
                                    .depth = entries[i].depth,
                                    .expandable = has_children(i),
                                    .expanded = entries[i].expanded};
          },
      .depth = {},
  });
  tree.set_on_expand([&tree](std::size_t index, bool expand) {
    entries[shown()[index]].expanded = expand;
    tree.rows_changed();
    std::println("{} {}.", expand ? "Expanded" : "Collapsed", entries[shown()[index]].name);
  });
  tree.set_on_select(
      [](std::size_t index) { std::println("Selected {}.", entries[shown()[index]].name); });
  tree.set_on_activate(
      [](std::size_t index) { std::println("Opened {}.", entries[shown()[index]].name); });

  host.frame();
  host.press_key(basalt::key::tab);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::end);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::up);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::right);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::down);
  host.press_key(basalt::key::enter);

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}

Uploader

An uploader collects files from a file dialog or from files that the user drops on it. It lists the files as removable chips. It holds paths only. Your program reads and sends the files.

Create and configure

Pass a name, an uploader_layout and an uploader_behavior to the constructor.

Layout Meaning
no_drop_zone Only the Select Files button. The widget accepts no drops.
compact A one-row drop zone with the prompt and the button side by side.
spacious A taller drop zone with the prompt above the button.
Behavior Meaning
immediate Files are handed over when chosen. Each chip is busy until you call finish.
deferred_single The uploader holds one file. A new file replaces it.
deferred_multiple The uploader holds files until your program asks for them.
  • set_accepted_suffixes({".png", ".txt"}) limits the file types. The comparison ignores case. An empty list accepts every file.
  • set_prompt and set_button_label change the texts.
  • add_files(paths) adds files as if the user chose them. It returns the paths that it took. A rejected file sets the error message.
  • files() returns the held paths in the order that they were added. clear() removes them.
  • finish(path, succeeded) ends an upload in the immediate behavior. A failure marks the chip as an error.
  • set_error_message sets the text below the chips. An empty text clears the error.
  • select_files() opens the file dialog from code.

The Select Files button calls the file_dialog of the tree. Set it with widget_tree::set_file_dialog. Without a dialog, the button does nothing.

Events

set_on_added calls its handler with the paths that the uploader took, after it lists them. set_on_removed calls its handler with the path of a file that the user removed. While files are dragged over the drop zone, dragging() is true and the zone shows the drag state.

Example

The program examples/widgets/uploader.cpp makes an uploader that accepts PNG and text files. It adds two accepted files and one rejected file, and prints the held files and the error message.

// An uploader that accepts PNG and text files. The program adds two accepted files and one rejected
// file.

#include <print>

#include "example_host.h"

auto main(int argc, char **argv) -> int {
  auto host = example::example_host{{420, 200}};

  auto &files = host.content().emplace_child<basalt::uploader>("Attachments");
  files.set_prompt("Drop files here");
  files.set_accepted_suffixes({".png", ".txt"});
  files.set_on_added([](std::vector<std::string> const &paths) {
    std::println("{} file(s) were added.", paths.size());
  });
  host.content().set_cross_alignment(basalt::alignment::stretch);

  host.frame();
  files.add_files({"notes.txt", "photo.png", "program.exe"});
  host.frame();
  std::println("The uploader holds {} file(s).", files.files().size());
  std::println("The error message is \"{}\".", files.error_message());

  return host.finish(argc, argv);
}
